new_or_updated_candidates.mechanism: Locally coupled convolutional recurrent dynamics use traveling-wave-like temporal evolution to expand effective receptive fields and encode global spatial context; a readout over the hidden-state time series converts the propagated dynamics into a segmentation representation.
evidence: Published in the CCN 2025 Proceedings; arXiv 2502.06034 and public author code are available.

Foreground-only MNIST, ten seeds: Neural Wave Machine (NWM) Linear, 177k parameters, FG-Acc 0.90±0.02, FG-IoU 0.85±0.04, FG-Loss 0.30±0.07. A 16-layer local CNN with 193k parameters reaches 0.57±0.39, 0.50±0.35, 1.73±1.80; a convolutional LSTM Linear with 151k reaches 0.79±0.28, 0.73±0.26, 0.78±1.25.

Foreground-only Tetrominoes, ten seeds: the same family of time-series recurrent readouts reaches approximately 0.99 foreground accuracy for NWM Linear, while the strongest listed local CNN (8 layers, 173k parameters) reaches 0.74±0.26 FG-Acc and 0.64±0.22 FG-IoU.

Multi-MNIST foreground metrics: NWM Linear with about 55k parameters reaches 0.96±0.01 FG-Acc and 0.93±0.01 FG-IoU; U-Net 3-level with about 69k reaches 0.90±0.10 and 0.87±0.13, while larger U-Nets reach 0.97-0.98 foreground accuracy.

Temporal readout matters strongly: on MNIST NWM Last is 0.50±0.08 FG-Acc versus NWM Linear 0.90±0.02; LSTM Last is 0.32±0.23 versus LSTM Linear 0.79±0.28. This supports use of the evolving trajectory rather than only the final recurrent state.

On the polygons task, the fraction of spatial locations assigned longer estimated wavelengths co-varies with improving model loss during training with correlation coefficient 0.961 averaged over five random seeds.

The paper reports that standard convolutional LSTMs, which lack the NWM's explicit wave-biased initialization, also develop visually wave-like hidden dynamics under the local-connectivity task constraint.
The public repository KempnerInstitute/traveling-waves-integrate includes code and result-oriented directories/scripts for reproducing the reported experiments.
mechanistic_scope: The evidence is strong for temporal local recurrence as an efficient route to spatial integration on synthetic segmentation tasks, but it is not a clean proof that traveling waves themselves are uniquely causal.

No matched intervention that destroys wave propagation while preserving parameter count, local recurrence and optimization was recovered in this run; wavelength/performance correlation and emergent LSTM waves are suggestive rather than causal isolation.
The tasks are Polygons/MNIST/Tetrominoes/Multi-MNIST-style vision segmentation rather than language, audio, control, or long-context agent benchmarks.
Training is conventional gradient-based learning; the neuroscience transfer concerns architecture/dynamics, not a biologically local learning rule.
Foreground-only metrics and all-pixel metrics appear in different paper tables/versions; they must not be mixed when comparing reported numbers.

deferred.lead: Information dynamics and Memory in Neural Networks through Fisher Information Diffusion (ICML 2026)
deferred.mechanism: Dynamic mean-field/Fisher-information diffusion characterizes how input information propagates through recurrent subpopulations; memory requires not just critical spectral radius but alignment of input structure with stable information-propagating subspaces. The work proposes a Fisher-optimal initialization.
evidence_recovered: ICML 2026's official downloads index lists the paper as accepted.

The earlier public manuscript reports a tanh-RNN copy task with 100 neurons, delay 50 and ten recurrent subpopulations, and sequential-MNIST with fixed recurrent weights/readout-only training; supplementary text also reports CIFAR-10/IndoorCVPR and an LSTM-gate application where Fisher initialization trains faster/higher than standard initializations.
Exact final-version numeric accuracies/losses were not recovered in this run, so it is not promoted to the quantified candidate set yet.
